# 1 Chronicles Chapter 20 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 380v–381r

---

**1** In the spring of the year, the time when kings go out to battle, Joab led out the army and ravaged the land of the Ammonites. He came and besieged Rabbah. But David remained in Jerusalem. Joab struck Rabbah and overthrew it.

**2** David took the crown from the head of their king. He found that it weighed a talent of gold and that there was a precious stone set in it. It was placed on David's head. He also carried off a great amount of plunder from the city.

**3** He brought out the people who were in it and set them to labor with saws, iron picks, and axes. David did the same to all the cities of the Ammonites. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

**4** After this, war broke out with the Philistines at Gezer. At that time Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Sippai, one of the descendants of the giants, and the Philistines were subdued.

**5** There was again war with the Philistines, and Elhanan the son of Jair struck down Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.

**6** There was again war at Gath, where there was a man of great stature who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot — twenty-four in number. He also was descended from the giants.

**7** When he taunted Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimea, David's brother, struck him down.

**8** These were descended from the giants in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verse 1 — The Omission of Bathsheba:** The Chronicler's most striking editorial decision. The parallel passage in 2 Samuel 11:1 begins identically — "In the spring of the year, the time when kings go out" — and then narrates David's adultery with Bathsheba and the murder of Uriah. The Chronicler skips from the departure of the army to the fall of Rabbah, omitting 2 Samuel 11:2–12:25 entirely. This silence speaks volumes about the Chronicler's theological purpose: David is the temple-preparer, and that portrait must remain unblemished.

**Verse 5 — The Goliath problem:** 2 Samuel 21:19 says Elhanan killed "Goliath the Gittite." 1 Samuel 17 says David killed Goliath. The Chronicler harmonizes: Elhanan killed "Lahmi, the brother of Goliath." Whether this reflects an independent tradition or editorial harmonization is debated.

**Verse 6 — Twenty-four digits:** The detail of the six-fingered, six-toed warrior is one of the Bible's most vivid physical descriptions. Polydactyly (extra digits) is a real genetic condition. The Chronicler preserves this detail from 2 Samuel 21:20 without alteration.

*— LOGOS*
